provenance: Written 2026-09-23 from RGW option defaults at v19.2.6/v20.2.4, Ceph CVE pages, trackers 79674/79698/70040/70736/73348, Rook docs at v1.20.7 and master, ceph-users 2026-08-31.

evals.name: restic-presigned-broke
evals.prompt: After upgrading our Rook RGW from Ceph 19.2.5 to 19.2.6, restic backups to the Ceph S3 endpoint started failing with 403 SignatureDoesNotMatch on uploads; other tools like s5cmd still work. What changed and what can I do right now?
evals.expected_output: CVE-2026-54330 SigV4 hardening; unsigned Content-Type on presigned PUT rejected (tracker 79674); workaround rgw_sigv4_insecure true until 19.2.7/20.2.5; it reopens the CVE, scope and remove later.
assertions: Attributes the failure to the SigV4 hardening fix for CVE-2026-54330 in 19.2.6
Gives the workaround ceph config set client.rgw rgw_sigv4_insecure true (or equivalent Rook config)
Says the workaround should be removed once a fixed release (19.2.7 / 20.2.5) is running, or that it weakens the CVE fix

evals.name: multisite-403-after-upgrade
evals.prompt: Rook multisite RGW, two zones in one zonegroup. After upgrading both clusters to Ceph 20.2.4, creating a bucket via the secondary zone endpoint returns 403 AccessDenied. We already set rgw_sigv4_insecure=true on both, still broken. Fix?
evals.expected_output: Tracker 79698: RGW's own forwarding rejected; need both rgw_sigv4_insecure true AND rgw_s3_client_max_sig_ver 2 in each zone; revert after fixed release.
assertions: Explains RGW's own inter-zone forwarded requests are rejected by the hardened SigV4 validation
States rgw_sigv4_insecure alone is not enough and rgw_s3_client_max_sig_ver must be set to 2 as well
Says to revert both settings (false / -1) once all zones run a fixed release

evals.name: aws-sdk-checksum-squid
evals.prompt: Our Python app upgraded boto3 to the latest and now PutObject to our Ceph RGW (Squid 19.2.6) sometimes fails with InvalidRequest / checksum errors. It worked with the old boto3. We can't upgrade Ceph to Tentacle this quarter. What's the fix?
evals.expected_output: New AWS SDK default checksums; RGW lacks CRC64NVME before Tentacle; set request/response checksum calculation to when_required; Squid backport not shipped.
assertions: Attributes it to the AWS SDK change that sends checksums by default on every supported request
Recommends setting request checksum calculation to when_required (AWS_REQUEST_CHECKSUM_CALCULATION or botocore config) as the fix
States CRC64NVME support arrived in Tentacle and is not available in Squid (no shipped backport)

evals.name: large-omap-index
evals.prompt: HEALTH_WARN 1 large omap objects, and it's in the rgw buckets.index pool. One bucket has ~12 million objects. What do I do, and why doesn't the warning go away right after I fix it?
evals.expected_output: Index shard over 200000 key threshold; bucket limit check; reshard to more shards; warning clears after next deep scrub; dynamic resharding default 100000 objs/shard.
assertions: Identifies a bucket index shard exceeding the large-omap key threshold (200000 keys)
Recommends radosgw-admin bucket limit check and resharding the bucket (radosgw-admin bucket reshard --num-shards)
Explains the warning only clears after the next deep scrub of the affected PG (or suggests triggering a deep scrub)

evals.name: lifecycle-not-running
evals.prompt: I set an S3 lifecycle rule on a Ceph RGW bucket to expire objects after 1 day. It's 2pm, objects are 3 days old, nothing got deleted. Is lifecycle broken? And after they do get deleted, why doesn't pool usage drop?
evals.expected_output: LC runs only in rgw_lifecycle_work_time 00:00-06:00; lc list / lc process; GC delays tail deletion 2h min wait.
assertions: Explains lifecycle runs only during rgw_lifecycle_work_time (default 00:00-06:00)
Mentions radosgw-admin lc list and/or lc process to inspect or run it now
Explains garbage collection delays freeing tail data (rgw_gc_obj_min_wait, 2h) so usage drops later

evals.name: rgw-accounts-rook
evals.prompt: We want AWS-style IAM accounts on our Rook Ceph object store (Rook v1.20.7, Ceph 19.2.6) so teams manage their own users and policies. I saw CephObjectStoreAccount in the docs — can we use it in production?
evals.expected_output: Experimental; only works with ceph-ci main image; not on released Ceph; alternatives.
assertions: States CephObjectStoreAccount is experimental
States it only works with the Ceph main/CI image (quay.ceph.io/ceph-ci/ceph:main), not with released Ceph like 19.2.6
Does not recommend it for production on this stack

evals.name: reshard-stale-multisite
evals.prompt: Multisite RGW. radosgw-admin reshard stale-instances list shows hundreds of stale bucket instances. Can I just run radosgw-admin reshard stale-instances rm to clean up?
evals.expected_output: No: docs say not in multisite.
assertions: Says not to run stale-instances rm in a multisite deployment
Cites the Ceph documentation's warning against stale-instance cleanup in multisite

evals.name: tentacle-lastmodified
evals.prompt: After upgrading RGW from Squid to Tentacle, our rclone sync job suddenly thinks thousands of objects changed and re-uploads them, even though nothing changed. Any known behaviour change?
evals.expected_output: Tentacle truncates LastModified to seconds for AWS parity; mtimes appear different; rclone compares modtime; use size/checksum or --modify-window.
assertions: Identifies that Tentacle truncates S3 LastModified timestamps to the second
Connects this to sync tools comparing modification times and suggests a mitigation (e.g. compare by size/checksum or a modify-window)

evals.name: bypass-gc-copyobject
evals.prompt: Need to delete a huge bucket fast on our Squid RGW. Planning radosgw-admin bucket rm --bucket=big --purge-objects --bypass-gc. Many objects in other buckets were created by server-side copy from this one. Any risk?
evals.expected_output: Tracker 73348: bypass-gc with server-side copies corrupts shared tail objects; avoid bypass-gc.
assertions: Warns that --bypass-gc can corrupt/delete data of objects created by server-side CopyObject that share tail objects
Recommends not using --bypass-gc here (use normal GC deletion)
